flashcard_questions.q: What type of wave are all electromagnetic waves?
At what speed do all electromagnetic waves travel through a vacuum?
Which equation links wave speed, frequency and wavelength?
flashcard_questions.a: wave speed = frequency × wavelength, or v = f × λ

flashcard_questions.q: The spectrum in order: radio → ____ → infrared → visible → ____ → X-rays → gamma
Which type of electromagnetic wave has the longest wavelength and lowest frequency?
Which type of electromagnetic wave is the most penetrating and most strongly ionising?
What happens to the wavelength of an electromagnetic wave as its frequency rises?
Why can a radio signal be received when the transmitter is not in sight?
flashcard_questions.a: The waves diffract around hills and buildings.

flashcard_questions.q: How does a microwave oven heat food?
flashcard_questions.a: The waves are absorbed by water molecules in the food, making them vibrate.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of electromagnetic wave does a thermal imaging camera detect?
Which electromagnetic radiation makes the skin produce vitamin D?
Which cancer risk rises with overexposure to ultraviolet radiation?
What does it mean to say that a radiation is ionising?
flashcard_questions.a: It can knock electrons out of atoms, creating ions that damage cells and DNA.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do bones show up white on an X-ray image?
flashcard_questions.a: Bone absorbs X-rays far more than soft tissue does, so fewer reach the detector.
